articleTitle: Research on UAV Position Adjustment Based on Local Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In azimuth-only passive UAV positioning system, the UAV that deviates from the ideal position cannot be located by geometric algorithm. In this paper, a local optimal algorithm is proposed, which first confirms that some UAVs are in the optimal position, establishes the positioning model, and obtains the local optimal solution. Then, using the position relationship between UAVs, the position of other UAVs is obtained through traversing, and the local optimal solution is used to achieve global optimization. Finally, the error detection function is established to test the feasibility of the method. The results show that the local optimal model can be used to optimize the position of UAVs, and the error is small, which is simple and practical.

articleTitle: Scattering Characterization Method for Space Targets Based on GEO Spacecrafts
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: When it is difficult to obtain spacecraft visible light images, photometric data become the most important optical data in airspace sensing. In recent years, although many intelligent recognition algorithms have been successfully applied to spacecraft recognition, people cannot fully utilize the traditional photometric data for spacecraft characterization due to its single data form. In this paper, a new data form is proposed, i.e., presenting photometric data in the form of two-dimensional heat map images. This new data form is based on the observational geometric relationship between the Sun, the spacecraft and the station, and is able to clearly reflect the pointing, number, size and shape of the spacecraft specular reflection components.

articleTitle: Proof and Application of a Civil Aircraft Balance Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In contemporary aircraft design projects, stability analysis and verification of control law design are often completed through simulation of aircraft models. The simulation initialization of aircraft models generally requires the aircraft to be in a balanced state of uniform linear motion in the air. At this time, it is necessary to calculate the required aircraft attitude angle for this equilibrium state as input for the simulation. At the same time, the attitude angle and control surface deviation of the aircraft in a balanced state of uniform linear motion in the air are also important indicators for evaluating the flight quality of the aircraft, and are also important basis for control law design. This article provides a detailed introduction to a newly designed algorithm for calculating the balance state of aircraft. The algorithm has been rigorously mathematically proven to have extremely high accuracy and can be used for flight simulation, flight quality calculation, control law design, and other work.

articleTitle: Research on Health Monitoring Method of Integrated Modular Avionics System Based on Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA) system is an important part of aircraft, it is related to the reliability and safety of the entire aircraft. Therefore, its health monitoring is an essential and important link. Taking IMA as the research object, this paper firstly presents a method of constructing IMA health detection index system. Secondly, based on IMA architecture and partition operation mechanism, the system health monitoring model is constructed by using Bayesian network. At the same time, in order to overcome the problem that the engineering amount of constructing Bayesian network system model parameters increases exponentially with the increase of the number of parent nodes, a method of constructing Bayesian network model parameters based on cloud mode is provided. Finally, the simulation verifies that the health monitoring method based on Bayesian network can effectively analyze the health status of IMA under each monitoring index.

articleTitle: Design of Servo Control System Based on DSP and FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Solid rocket motors are often applied in the power system of aircrafts because of not relying on external oxygen during operation. Through the collaborative work of multiple servo mechanisms on a solid rocket motor, thrust vector control of an aircraft can be achieved. In response to requirements of the high dynamic and high precision for the thrust vector synthesis, a servo control system scheme based on DSP and FPGA is designed and studied in this paper. In the main hardware design scheme, DSP is utilized as the main control chip, FPGA is selected as the auxiliary control chip, and the controller area network is adopted as the communication bus among driver modules. System control architecture and the profile position mode of the driver module are briefly introduced. A three-closed PID control algorithm is conducted in the control strategy, and a low-pass filter is performed in the speed loop for estimating the motor speed to reduce the measurement noise interference. A prototype based on the four-axis drive scheme is implemented, and the experimental results show that the dead time of step response is independent of the motion distance for mechanisms and is less than 5 ms. Moreover, the steady-state error is less than 0.05 mm, achieving high-precision motion control.

articleTitle: A Efficient Radar Signal Recognition Method Based on Phase Difference Rearrangement
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The current electromagnetic environment is complex, and the signal received by the reconnaissance generally has the problem of low signal-to-noise ratio. Aiming at the problem that the recognition performance of radar emitter signal recognition method based on traditional statistical features for complex modulation signal types is generally not high under low signal-to-noise ratio, this paper proposes a fast recognition method of radar emitter signal based on phase difference rearrangement processing. This method further performs phase difference rearrangement processing on the extracted instantaneous phase by extracting the instantaneous phase characteristics of the signal, and obtains the characterization of the signal in the transform domain. Finally, combined with the convolutional neural network, the phase characteristics after differential rearrangement processing are used as the input of the convolutional neural network, so as to realize the rapid identification of radar emitter signals. In this paper, seven kinds of modulation signals are used for simulation experiments under different signal-to-noise ratios. The recognition accuracy can reach 91.7 % when the signal-to-noise ratio is-5dB, and the recognition accuracy is close to 98 % when the signal-to-noise ratio is 0dB. With the improvement of signal-to-noise ratio, it can reach 100 % under high signal-to-noise ratio. The experiment can verify that the proposed method has the advantages of high accuracy and good robustness.

articleTitle: Aerospace Equipment Safety Evaluation and Key Factor Analysis Method Considering Performance Degradation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the performance degradation of the equipment represented by aircraft after long-term storage leads to the occurrence of safety accidents, this paper carries out the research on the aerospace equipment safety evaluation and key factor analysis method considering performance degradation. Firstly, based on the mature fault tree analysis method, the safety logic analysis of the product is realized. Then, a product performance degradation model considering the generalized stress under the mission profile is established, and the accurate analysis of the basic event failure rate is realized. On this basis, the fault tree is transformed into a Bayesian network model according to the transformation principle. Through the coupling analysis of reliability and safety, dynamic safety evaluation and key factor analysis are achieved, solving the problem of long-term storage safety evaluation and risk element control of aerospace equipment. Finally, a case study is carried out, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified.

articleTitle: Pressure Calibration of Tower Fly by and GPS Methods and Error Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: New aircrafts' pressure system need to be calibrated to obtain accurate airspeed and altitude, which is also required by airworthiness regulations. Due to the different testing principles, different pressure calibration methods have different accuracies. In this paper, the tower fly by method and GPS method are used to calibrate the pressure of small transport aircraft, and the corresponding data processing methods are proposed. The test research shows that the results of GPS method are closer to the values specified in the flight manual, the accuracy is higher. The reading error of the two methods is compared and analyzed, and it is found that the reading error has less influence on the GPS results. The results of the deviation caused by conditional errors are compared and analyzed, and it is found that the altitude deviation has a greater influence on the tower fly by method, and the airspeed and wind speed deviation have a greater influence on the GPS method. Through quantitative analysis, the technical error allowable value is given, within whitch results of flight test can be ensure trustworthiness.

articleTitle: Research on the Application of Heat Switch in Thermal Management of Electronic Devices in Near Space
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Near space is located on the junction of sky and space, which is the key field of future development of aerospace technology. The ambient temperature of near space changes greatly, and the minimum temperature can reach -88°C, which is far beyond the operating temperature of electronic devices. The thermal design of electronic devices needs to be taken both heat dissipation and thermal insulation into account, which requires weight and power resources. In order to save the resources of weight, space and power, the study of adaptive heat switch is conducted, which includes the integration design method of heat pipe and thermal insulation material, and the design method of adaptive temperature control unit based on heat pipe switch. Due to the heat pipe's characteristics of starting temperature, the temperature control unit can switch the heat dissipation or heat preservation mode according to the ambient temperature. The simulation and test results show that the heat switch can effectively cut off the thermal conductivity channel at low temperature to achieve good insulation effect without affecting the heat dissipation performance at high temperature.

articleTitle: A Prognostic Model Based on Binary Feature Fusion for Remaining Useful Life of Aircraft Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: To improve the prediction performance of the remaining service life of aircraft engines, a binary feature fusion prediction method is proposed, taking into account the inclusion of different degradation information in different features, and to avoid mutual interference between mixed inputs and fully utilize degradation information. Firstly, a multi head self attention mechanism is used to extract degraded information between features and automatically learn the weights of different features. Then, a multi-channel convolutional neural network is used to extract the internal degradation information from each feature. Next, the binary degradation feature is nonlinearly fused through the fully connected layer, and the GRU network is used to predict its remaining service life. Validation was conducted on the publicly available dataset C-MAPSS, and compared with other methods, the results showed that the method decreased by about 8% and 10% on the RMSE and Score evaluation indicators, respectively.

articleTitle: CFD Investigation of Crew Oxygen Cylinder Leakage Concentration in Triangle Area of Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A computational model applied with RANS turbulence is developed to solve the oxygen leakage concentration distribution problem in the triangle area of civil aircraft during a cruise. We consider a steady-state simulation of oxygen leakage. We have a concentration distribution investigation in three different directions of the triangle area, illustrating the effects of the ventilation system. Results show that more than 25% of the oxygen concentration is mainly concentrated in the small area of the leakage port of the unit's oxygen cylinder regulator and the area under the floor. This means the ventilation system can effectively and quickly dilute the high concentration oxygen.

articleTitle: Research on Structural Response Modeling Method for Flutter Flight Test Under Sweep Excitation of Control Surface Based on Volterra Series
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Sweep excitation of control surface is the most commonly used excitation method in flutter test flight. The Structural response under excitation has become the key analysis data in flutter test flight. Therefore, the modeling method of structural vibration response under sweep excitation of control surface in aircraft flutter test flight is studied, which can realize the prediction of structural vibration response and support flutter test flight. A modeling method of aeroelastic response based on Volterra kernel is proposed to realize the vibration response modeling of structure excited by sweep frequency of flutter test flight control surface. The Volterra kernel model of structural vibration response excited by sweep excitation of control surface is established. Based on the sweep excitation of control surface input and structural vibration response output, the Volterra kernel model of aircraft structural vibration response excited by sweep excitation of control surface is identified. The effectiveness of this method is verified by using the simulation data of pitching, sinking and floating aeroelastic system and aircraft flutter flight test data, which provides support for predicting the vibration response of structure excited by sweep excitation of control surface. The maximum peak error of the model response identified of the simulation system is 3.72%. The maximum peak error of flight test data identification model response is 5.65%.

articleTitle: Conformal Geometric Algebraic Description of Flight Collision Detection Algorithm Based on Cylinder Protection Zone
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In order to provide sufficient reaction time for air traffic controllers and pilots, a Flight Conflict Detection Algorithm (FCDA) based on Cylindrical Protection Zone (CPZ) in the Conformal Geometric Algebra (CGA) is proposed. Initially, the CGA description of the CPZ is represented by using the CGA forms of the central circle and central axis segments of the cylinder. Then based on the inner and outer product and geometric product operations of CGA, the positional relationship of the two CPZs is judged to determine whether a flight conflict occurs or not. Subsequently, we compared the performance of flight conflict detection methods based on rectangular protection zones, spherical protection zones, and cylindrical protection zones through experiments in CGA and Euclidean space, respectively, the experimental results show that in CGA, the proposed method has a faster speed than the flight conflict method based on cuboids, and is basically equivalent to the method based on spherical protection zones. Significantly, all CGA-based methodologies demonstrated superior speed over their Euclidean space counterparts. Considering the propensity of rectangular and spherical zones to elicit false alarms due to their expansive coverage of airspace, the CGA-CPZ-FCDA method emerges as the superior choice.

articleTitle: Design, Analyze, and Simulation of a Bionic Swept-Back Wing Scheme with Force Amplification Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Compared with traditional aircraft, the variant aircraft can change the shape of its fuselage or wing to adapt to the needs of different flight conditions. Among them, the variable swept-back wing can provide excellent aerodynamic characteristics for the morphing aircraft by adjusting the swept back angle of the wing. Aiming at the problem of the existing variable swept-back wings encroach on the belly space. Based on the principles of mechanism and bionics, this paper innovatively puts forward a design scheme of wing root bending variable swept-wing without encroaching on the belly space and designs a force amplification mechanism, which is reasonable according to the principle of virtual work. It is verified to be able to amplify the force by 130% through a set of eigenvalues. It provides certain references for the design of the variable swept-back wing.

articleTitle: Top-Level Modeling and Simulation of Civil Aircraft Fly-by-Wire Flight Control System for Airworthiness Compliance Verification in Virtual Flight Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: With the advancement of computer technology, Virtual Flight Testing (VFT) methods have gradually integrated into the early validation activities of the civil aircraft product Iifecycle, becoming a mainstream approach in product development. Addressing issues such as inconsistent understanding in traditional document-based methods and weak correlation between requirements and validation activities, this paper focuses on the civil aircraft Fly-by-Wire (FBW) Flight Control System and proposes a top-level modeling and integrated simulation method for airworthiness validation in virtual flight testing. Firstly, starting from the descriptions in airworthiness regulations, we construct activity models for flight testing verification oriented towards compliance and quantitative constraint models. Secondly, we clarify the static structure, dynamic activities, and parameter constraint relationships within the system, establishing the top-level architecture model of the system. Subsequently, we create low-level simulation models for each unit within the system and achieve the correlation between the top-level and low-level models, thereby constructing a virtual integrated simulation environment based on SysML & Simulink. Finally, with the support of the virtual integrated simulation environment, we achieve real-time virtual simulation based on flight testing verification activities and automatic validation of airworthiness compliance. Experimental results demonstrate the system's compliance with the example airworthiness regulations, validating the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Smart System of Cabin Pressure Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The proper control and maintenance of cabin pressure are critical for ensuring the safety, comfort, and well-being of passengers and cabin crew aboard an aircraft. In this paper, we present the design and simulation of a smart system for cabin pressure control, the proposed system integrates advanced sensing technologies, intelligent neural network algorithm combined with PID control algorithm to optimize cabin pressure regulation during all phases of flight. The smart system utilizes a combination of pressure sensors and airflow sensors to continuously monitor the cabin environment, furthermore, in this paper, the modulation and simulation of the designed system has also been given.

articleTitle: Airport Runway Conflict Detection And Visual Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In order to prevent runway intrusion events due to the incorrect deployment of aircraft by controllers with insufficient situational awareness, a 3D visual simulation system for runway conflict detection is designed. By analyzing different types of conflict scenarios of aircraft arrival and departure, the runway conflict models are constructed, and for different conflict models, the spatial distance method is used to determine whether runway incursion of the aircraft occurs. Then the combination of spatial distance and time threshold are used for the conflict alarm. The runway protection area is constructed, the aircraft motion model of the airport surface is established based on the data of airport surveillance data. The visual simulation of the arrival and departure conflict detection algorithm is realized on the Unreal Engine 4 platform. The experimental results show that according to the arrival and departure conflict detection, when aircrafts are close to each other and less than the encounter time threshold, the system can detect the runway conflict in real time and give the alarm.

articleTitle: A Study of Data Processing and Error Analysis in Airspeed Calibration Using GPS Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Airspeed calibration is the prerequisite for aircraft to obtain accurate airspeed and altitude, and it is the most basic and fundamental test flight subject of aircraft. In this paper, GPS trilateral method is used to calibrate airspeed, and the formulas for solving true airspeed and speed and pressure errors are introduced in detail. On the basis of the original airspeed calibration results, the error analysis is given, and more accurate and reliable pressure error results are obtained by means of mathematical analysis.

articleTitle: Study on Transfer Alignment Method for Nonlinear Filtered Inertial Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Aiming at the feature that the transfer alignment of inertial navigation system moving base is a nonlinear system in practical engineering, this paper establishes an accurate nonlinear filtering model for the transfer alignment of moving base by adopting the second-order Markov process to represent the dynamic deflection deformation in the process of transfer alignment and by applying the nonlinear filtering method to the process of transfer alignment of inertial navigation system. Finally, through the simulation comparison with the Kalman filtering method, the results show that the nonlinear filtering algorithm has obvious advantages in the alignment accuracy in the transfer alignment process of the inertial navigation system.

articleTitle: Real-Time Control of Intelligent Production Line for Automatic Assembly of Aerospace Products
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Due to the wide variety and small number of aerospace products, the assembly process of related products becomes very complicated. In order to achieve the production requirements of safer, more efficient, better production quality and higher resource utilization, we integrate the control system into the assembly line of aerospace products to make it automated. In order to further verify the feasibility of the system, we use 3D virtual reality visualization to design the onsite real-time operation system scheme.

articleTitle: Design of Milliarcsecond Attitude Control System for CHES Based on Telescope
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Closeby Habitable Exoplanet Survey (CHES) is a space precision optical survey satellite for extrasolar planetary systems with a high quality, low distortion, and high stability telescope as its primary payload. In order to ensure microarc-second astrometry accuracy and PSF stability during scientific exposure, the satellite platform needs to achieve a pointing accuracy of better than 0.07” and a pointing stability of 0.0036” /0.02s during scientific observations. This paper introduces the design of milliarcsecond high stability attitude control system of CHES satellite based on guide sensor. First, the key technical indicators of milliarcsecond high stability attitude control are decomposed, including the design index of load camera, the attitude determination index of high-precision guide sensor and the attitude stability control index of high-precision thruster. Secondly, the system scheme is introduced, including the composition of the system, the attitude measurement and determination method of the guide star sensor, the µN thruster and the high-precision attitude determination and control algorithm. Finally, the control results of attitude accuracy and high stability of the guide sensor are simulated and analyzed.

articleTitle: Experimental Study on Constant Stress Variable Range Reciprocating Compression of Composite Solid Propellant
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Solid rocket motor may be subjected to various loads during storage, which may lead to fatigue damage such as cracks and debonding of solid propellant. The unidirectional compressive mechanical properties of propellants were obtained by designing compressive fatigue damage specimens. The effects of constant stress range and fatigue loading frequency on compressive fatigue damage of composite solid propellant were studied through constant stress range and variable range reciprocating compression tests. The quantitative relationship equations among constant stress range, fatigue loading frequency and fatigue failure times are obtained by fitting test data.

articleTitle: Fault Tolerance Control for Asymmetric Failure of Distributed Electric Propulsion Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In this paper, a transition state compensation control method for distributed electric propulsion system is proposed for the asymmetric failure problem of electric aircraft, which takes into account thrust and yaw moment. The permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) model and the aircraft yaw moment mathematical model is established, and based on the yaw moment suffered by the aircraft, a variable command decision-making including yaw moment compensation term is established. Meanwhile, an instruction tracking control algorithm is designed for variable command decision making, and the parameters of the designed control algorithm are optimized by intelligent algorithm. The thrust-yaw moment cooperative compensation control after asymmetric failure of distributed electric propulsion (DEP) systems is completed through the fast response of electric propeller to compensate the aircraft yaw moment during the operating time of control surface. In this paper, MATLAB/Simulink simulation is carried out. The simulation results show that the proposed control method can accomplish the thrust response task of the electric propulsion system while reducing the yaw moment of the electric aircraft, which indicates the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Space Rendezvous Guidance Method for Non-Cooperative Targets Based on Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Facing the increasingly complex space environment, it is particularly important to approach and capture non cooperative space targets such as uncontrolled spacecraft. In order to solve the rendezvous guidance problem of continuous small-thrust non-cooperative space targets in near-circular orbits, a zero effort convex optimization guidance strategy was proposed by using the rolling convex optimization method and the rolling zero effort miss target distance estimation. It is suitable for both fixed time rendezvous tasks and adaptive time rendezvous tasks. The simulation results show that the fixed-time rendezvous task has a better rendezvous effect than the traditional differential countermeasure method, and the adaptive time rendezvous can complete the rendezvous task in a shorter time, and the method has stable performance and engineering application potential.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Trajectory Planning Method of Space Robot Based on Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: To solve the problems of poor stability, low movement efficiency and low precision of the drive joint during the movement of a space robot, a new drive joint trajectory planning method with optimal time-jerk constraint was proposed in this paper. Firstly, the kinematic model of the space robot is analyzed, and the kinematic relationship between the drive joints and the end effectors of the space robot is established. On this basis, according to the constraints of velocity, acceleration and secondary acceleration, the robot joint trajectory planning model was established with the optimal completion time-jerk as the optimization objective. Finally, based on the differential evolution algorithm, the adaptive control parameters and multi-population strategy in the algorithm are improved to solve the problems of large joint jitter and low motion efficiency in the process of optimal joint driving joint trajectory. The simulation results show that the proposed joint trajectory planning method can better solve the problems of large vibration, long time and poor stability in the process of space robot executing tasks.

articleTitle: Efficient EMI Effect Modeling of Antenna with Electromagnetic Wave Coupling Using Surface Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for electromagnetic interference (EMI) effect modeling of antenna with electromagnetic wave coupling by using surface integral equation (SIE) discretized with Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions. The EMI leads to the induced surface current on antenna and excites the scattered field. The induced current has no influence on the antenna input impedance, but it can affect the distribution of the far-field and currents. To monitor these changes, this interference can be approximated as a uniformly incident plane wave of a certain intensity, and the SIE with RWG basis is adopted here to simulate the electromagnetic field can current distribution of antenna. Numerical results are provided to show the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Effects of Camber and Thickness on the MAV Under the Mode of Multiple Degrees of Freedom
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: To investigate the influence of different wing thicknesses and cambers on the aerodynamic characteristics of Micro Air Vehicles (MAVs), a three-degree-of-freedom flapping model was established by developing a User-Defined Function (UDF). Utilizing Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) techniques, NACA series three-dimensional wings with varying cross-sectional shapes were chosen as the subjects of study. Employing both overlapping mesh and dynamic mesh techniques, lift and drag coefficients were computed. The results were analyzed in conjunction with pressure contour maps to explore their impact on the aerodynamic efficiency of MAVs. The findings indicate that the thickness and camber have minimal effects on the lift of the flapping aircraft but significantly enhance the drag and thrust. With an increase in thickness, the thrust augmentation reaches up to 50%, while the camber of the wing shape contributes to a thrust augmentation effect of approximately 60%.

articleTitle: Integrated Imaging Control Technology Based on the Multi-Channel Remote Sensing Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The camera control system plays a critical role in space remote sensing cameras, enabling the orderly deployment of internal camera resources, comprehensive management, and imaging control. This paper presents the system architecture of the camera control system for a multi-channel imaging camera in geostationary orbit. An integration technology that utilizes an integrated and dual-redundancy switch instruction SiP module and a multi-channel integrated telemetry acquisition SiP module is applied to meet high reliability redundancy requirements and lightweight design specifications. The development of automatic and interactive imaging control technology for multi-channel and multi-process is discussed, particularly for the intricate imaging process involving visible channels and multiple medium-wave infrared channels. Additionally, “shortcut” are incorporated to facilitate user interaction and streamline the imaging process. In conclusion, the camera control technology presented in this paper not only serves as an effective guarantee for achieving high system integration but also offers a solution for enhancing user convenience in operating complex camera systems. Furthermore, it provides a technical guide for the future development of space remote sensing camera control systems based on high system integration and automatic imaging control.

articleTitle: Virtual Assembly Evaluation and Optimization Decision Techniques for Large Planar Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A virtual assembly evaluation model is combined with a flatness compensation decision solver in order to offer the optimal compensation scheme for the large planar antennas assembly. The model focus on the actual measurement states of multiple installation sub-planes, as well as the local and overall assembly effects after compensation. The accuracy and effectiveness of this model have been fully demonstrated in the implementation and application of large-scale synthetic aperture radar antenna products.

articleTitle: Integrated Design of Guidance and Control for Hypersonic Vehicles Based on Disturbance Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This paper focuses on the challenge of designing an effective guidance and control system for the dive phase of hypersonic vehicles. To address this, an integrated approach is proposed, grounded in the principle of disturbance compensation. Firstly, a comprehensive guidance and control model is developed for hypersonic vehicles, which is founded on the motion model of the vehicle itself and the relative motion model describing the interaction between the vehicle and its target. Secondly, to compensate for the uncertainties in the model, a nonlinear disturbance observer is employed. The backstepping dynamic surface method is then utilized to complete the design of the integrated guidance and control system for hypersonic vehicles. Additionally, an appropriate Lyapunov function is selected to conduct a stability analysis of the system. In conclusion, simulations are carried out to validate the efficacy and resilience of the integrated guidance and control method proposed.

articleTitle: Explosive Containment Test Technology of the Transport Aircraft Battery Pack
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: the battery pack is an indispensable emergency power supply equipment for transport aircraft. The conformity verification of the battery pack for transport aircraft is the important contents of product development and airworthiness safety, the explosive containment verification test of the battery pack is of particular concern to the reviewer for its destructiveness, unrepeatability and high risk. The battery pack is designed with one-way valve and vent hole, and there is no reference containment test procedure applicable to the battery pack which are not sealed or which have apertures in the case and lid. In this paper, the containment test procedure of the transport aircraft battery pack is studied from two aspects of engineering test and airworthiness verification, and the test verification is completed by taking the cadmium nickel battery pack of a certain type of aircraft as an example. The results show that the containment procedure of the designed is reasonable and feasible, and can verify the compliance of the transport aircraft battery pack to the airworthiness standard in the explosion environment. The test procedures, methods and results are approved by the reviewer. The containment test procedure and technology formed can provide strong support for the subsequent containment test of the transportation aircraft battery pack.

articleTitle: RUL Prediction of Turbo Engine Based on CNN-LSTM and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In the process of equipment Remaining Useful Life (RUL), there are often high-dimensional, long-time series of correlation data. The traditional method is difficult to extract the characteristics of such data, and there are often problems such as the disappearance of gradient. For such cases, this article proposes a residual life prediction model for turbo engines based on CNN-LSTM ATTENTION. Preprocess the sensor data such as standardization, extract relevant features through CNN, and introduce attention mechanism to the traditional LSTM for practical feature extraction and prediction. The validation on C-MAPSS data set shows that this method achieves good prediction results.

articleTitle: Analysis of Lightning Ignition Source in Typical Wing Fuel Tank
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In order to alleviate the space tension in the wing and ensure a series of factors such as safety and airworthiness, this paper analyzes the safety of lightning ignition source of a model designed with two sets of hydraulic pipelines and one set of fuel pipelines in the wing fuel tank by means of simulation and test verification. It is found that there are relatively high density currents in the structural interface of the wing fuel tank and the connection between some pipelines and the clamp in the simulation. However, the calculated voltage on the pipeline is less than the threshold of spark generation. In order to explore the correctness of the simulation results, this paper conducted a lightning effect test study on the actual wing fuel tank restored by the one-to-one simulation model, and found that no spark appeared in the test, indicating that the three-casing design in the wing fuel tank can alleviate the space tension of the front and rear edges of the wing and avoid safety risks. It provides a technical reference for the lightning ignition source protection design of the subsequent aircraft fuel tank system.

articleTitle: Research on the Influence Factors of Ground Minimum Control Speed of Civil Aircraft Based on Dynamic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The ground minimum control speed (Vmcg) flight test is an essential high-risk test subject in civil aircraft flight testing. By establishing a dynamic simulation system, factors that affect the results of ground minimum control speed flight tests, such as engine failure speed, reaction time, rudder effect, weight, center of gravity (cg), etc., were studied. The impact of engine failure speed on the speed of aircraft trajectory recovery to be parallel to the runway centerline was analyzed, and the key points that should be paid attention to during flight tests were summarized, providing reference for civil aircraft ground minimum control speed flight tests.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Ring-Type Digitally Controlled Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Digitally controlled oscillator (DCO) plays an important role on all digital phase-locked loop (ADPLL). However, seldom DCO structure is applied to field programmable gate array (FPGA) hardware. This paper proposes a novel FPGA-based ring-DCO using a coarse adjustment module (CAM) and a fine adjustment module (FAM). The CAM adjusts the period of DCO by changing the number of inverters in the oscillation loop and obtains a large frequency range. Besides, the CAM applies an additional compensation block to fix irregular waveform. The FAM adjusts the number of low-delay buffers to obtain a small step size. The implemented ring-DCO has an adjustment step size of 0.541 ns and a frequency range of 6.89 MHz~142.369 MHz.

articleTitle: Air Traffic Control and Flight Management Systems Communication Interface for Four-Dimensional Trajectory Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The operational scenarios in airspace are becoming increasingly diverse and complex. Facilitating four-dimensional trajectory operations stands out as a prominent trend in the ongoing development of civil aviation transportation technology. The interaction and data exchange between Air Traffic Control (ATC) applications and Flight Management Systems (FMS) are essential to support these advanced trajectory operations. Based on the ARINC 656 specification, proposed a communication interface tailored for the Future Air Navigation System (FANS) 3/C and FMS to facilitate four-dimensional trajectory operations. The design has been validated, providing valuable guidance for the practical implementation of relevant technologies within the civil aviation.

articleTitle: Trajectory Tracking Control of Quadrotor Drones Based on Disturbance Observers
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A composite control method is proposed by combining a disturbance observer with sliding mode control to address the uncertainties of parameters, models and external disturbances in the position and attitude control system for quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The observer estimates the equivalent disturbances in real-time, and a sliding mode controller is designed based on these estimates to track the desired signals. The designed controller not only ensures the system's asymptotic stability but also effectively suppresses the impact of internal and external disturbances. Finally, simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Study on the Design of Anti-Shock Loading of Satellite-Borne Flexible Thin-Walled Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In the design process of satellite-borne electronic products, the shock response analysis of the product structure is a key step to improve its environmental adaptability. In this study, the frequency domain shock method was adopted to carry out satellite-borne flexible thin-walled antenna shock response simulation analysis and structural optimization design. We established the finite element model of this antenna. Through modal analysis, the intrinsic properties of the antenna structure were obtained. Subsequently, the shock response spectrum was applied to the antenna structure, to calculate the response of the antenna under shock loading, and the shock response, stress and deformation of the structure were obtained. Based on the simulation results, the design of the antenna structure was further optimized to achieve a balanced stress distribution. The shock simulation of the optimized antenna structure was conducted again to verify its stiffness and strength. The antenna's anti-shock vibration performance was verified by sine vibration and shock vibration tests. The results showed that the optimized antenna structure met the stiffness and strength design requirements and the shock-resistant environment demands. The study provides a theoretical basis and design reference for the shock-resistant design of satellite-borne electronic products.

articleTitle: An Innovative Optimization Framework for Aerodynamic Shape Optimization Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: It is necessary to optimize the design method of the airfoil aerodynamic shape for better performance while meeting the design requirements. However, current mainstream design methods for aerodynamic shape are based on CFD model simulations and rely heavily on manual experience design, which are very time-consuming. Therefore, we propose an innovative optimization framework based on multi-task learning for Aerodynamic Shape Optimization. Firstly, Bezier-ACGAN is used to intelligently parametrize the airfoil shape. Secondly, the MMOE-MF surrogate model is used to predict different-fidelity of aerodynamic data. Finally, GA optimizer selects the optimal shape that satisfies the optimization objective by adjusting the latent variables of Bezier-ACGAN. The performance of the proposed optimization framework is verified by two optimization design cases and results show that the predicted results of the optimal airfoils agree with the results of high-fidelity simulation well.

articleTitle: Application of Air-To-Ground Integration Technology in Civil Aircraft Engine AirStart Flight Test
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Engine airstart flight test is an essential flight test subject in civil aircraft flight test. Through the establishment of simplified Air-to-Ground Integrated System(ATGIS), the critical test point process of engine airstart is simulated in batches, and the control suggestions of critical test point are put forward; And based on the ATGIS, develop the air-to-ground comparative monitoring interface, assist ground monitoring personnel to judge the status of the engine, the results effectively support a certain type of civil aircraft engine airstart flight test, provide a reference for other types of civil aircraft engine airstart flight test.

articleTitle: Geometric Algebra Based Kalman Filter Trajectory Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: To improve the safety and efficiency of aviation operation, a Kalman filtered trajectory prediction algorithm based on geometric algebra is proposed in this space. Firstly, the Kalman filter equations for trajectory prediction in geometric algebraic space are given by taking position, velocity and acceleration as state variables and position, velocity and acceleration in a typical trajectory as observations. Secondly, the matrix operation in the geometric algebraic space is simplified to the matrix operation by establishing a composite geometric algebraic space. Then, the versor operator in the conformal geometric algebraic space is introduced into the Kalman filter, and the steps of geometric algebra-based Kalman filter trajectory prediction are given to improve the prediction rate and accuracy. The experimental results show that the proposed trajectory prediction algorithm has the highest accuracy and the operation efficiency is improved by 27.66<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> compared with the Kalman filter algorithm in Euclidean space and the DBSCAN clustering algorithm.

articleTitle: Control Allocation Design of Rudder of a Flying-Wing Aircraft with Fault Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The shortcomings of the flying-wing aircraft in terms of flight stability and handling performance are as prominent as its advantages in aerodynamics, stealth performance and fuselage space. How to control its shortcomings and give full play to its advantages is the purpose of this paper. In this paper, the application of the control allocation method in the rudder control of flying-wing aircraft with large aspect ratio is studied. An approximate linearization model of rudder effect was established according to each rudder effect to realize the linear control and allocation of rudder. Three linear allocation methods, namely the display combination method, the pseudo-inverse method and the reallocation pseudo-inverse method, are simulated and compared, respectively. When the actuator fails, the control distribution is automatically reconstructed by using the processing method of control allocation reconstruction, so that the flight control system still has a good control effect on the flying wing layout aircraft when the actuator fails.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Availability Analysis for Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Availability is a comprehensive reflection of product reliability. Availability factors should be paid attention to in the design, manufacture, operation and maintenance stages of civil aircraft systems and equipment, and availability of systems or equipment should be improved by optimizing design, strengthening maintenance time. Through studying the calculation method of availability index suitable for civil aircraft systems and equipment, and carrying out concrete analysis and application, it is helpful to carry out the balance between maintainability and reliability design scheme and index in different stages of civil aircraft, it can effectively improve the availability of systems or equipment, which is of great significance to improve product production efficiency, ensure flight safety and reduce operation costs.

articleTitle: Modified Relative Lambert Guidance Algorithm for Spacecraft Flyby Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: For achieving spacecraft flyby observation mission, obtaining a high-accuracy control method in closed form or with fast computation is necessary, attracting wide attention from many researchers. In this paper, a modified method based on relative motion control was proposed. It can improve the accuracy with accurate zero-effort-orbit propagators and achieve fast computation using analytical zero-effort-orbit propagators and a linearized relative-motion control solution, eliminating the error of the linearized relative-motion control model. Numerical examples show that the error of the method converges to the error of the zero-effort-orbit propagators. Compared with the previous method, it shows better accuracy, robustness, and computation efficiency. It is hoped the algorithm will be implemented in the spacecraft flyby observation mission involving a transfer with hundreds of kilometers.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Aircraft Thrust Reversers Based on QFD and AHP
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The QFD method is applied to the system design evaluation of the aircraft nacelle thrust reverser. Based on the top-level requirements and quality characteristics during the design phase, manufacturing phase, and utilization phase, a detailed analysis is conducted, and quality houses for each phase are constructed for quality function deployment. The AHP method is introduced to calculate the importance of typical requirements, combining expert ratings to obtain a competitive evaluation of requirements and the relevance of typical quality characteristics. This establishes a scientific evaluation system for the design, manufacturing, and usage phases of the nacelle thrust reverser with different emphasis and attention. Using the design of a domestic thrust reverser as an example, a comparison is made with foreign competitive models of the same type. The strengths and weaknesses of the thrust reverser are analyzed, and improvement directions are proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Performance of Distributed Thermoelectric Cooling System Based on High-Power Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Rapid Maneuver Space Application System (RMSAS) needs to adapt to different working modes and orbits. Most spacecraft thermal control is realized by primary passive thermal control and auxiliary active thermal control, which is suitable for long-term on-orbit satellites and its platform that has stable operation, but it is incapable of carrying out rapid missions through the space platform due to the lack of flexibility, rapidity and adjustment ability. Therefore, a more flexible thermal control system is needed. This paper proposes a distributed thermoelectric cooling system based on high-power device to meet the temperature control requirements of high-power device for RMSAS. Specifically, the steady-state mathematical models of distributed thermoelectric cooling system are established through the application of energy conservation law, the combined performance of different distribauted thermoelectric cooling systems are analyzed under steady-state comparison, which provides a designing approach for the rapid temperature control of space high-power equipment

articleTitle: Lyapunov-Based Backstepping Model Predictive Control for Quadrotors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In recent years, quadrotors have received attention from a wide range of scholars. For the flight control of quadrotors, trajectory tracking control is particularly important. This paper introduces a Lyapunov-based backstepping model predictive control (LBMPC) method to address the quadrotor trajectory tracking problem under input saturation. Firstly, the mathematical formulation of the quadrotor is introduced, and the position model and attitude model are written separately. For the position controller, the backstepping control is adopted, while for the attitude controller, the Lyapunov-based model predictive control is used. Then, the stability of the system using the LBMPC is demonstrated. Finally, the simulation results show that LBMPC is able to complete the trajectory tracking task with input saturation.

articleTitle: Topographic Avoidance Track Planning Under Complex Terrain Based on the Optimized A * -Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: For the needs of complex terrain aircraft track planning, This paper presents an optimized A * -genetic algorithm to solve the-problem of terrain avoidance track planning based on the aircraft carrier performance of the aircraft itself and environmental threat constraints. First, the performance of the aircraft is constrained and modeling, and the environment of the complex terrain is modeling. Secondly, the traditional genetic algorithm is improved, mainly in the process of crossing and variation, the A * algorithm based on Dubins path improvement is introduced to generate subpaths, and the elite retention strategy is adopted to prevent the loss of excellent individuals of one generation; meanwhile, the weighting function is introduced in the fitness function to realize terrain avoidance. Finally, the simulation confirmed that the optimized A * -genetic algorithm can perform effective terrain avoidance track planning.

articleTitle: LEO Constellation Cooperative On-board Processing Framework: Modeling and Solution
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Satellite technology has advanced significantly, pri-marily in terms of miniaturization and intelligent capabilities. These advancements have facilitated the development of larger and more sophisticated satellites, which now enable on-board data processing. However, the dynamic topology and limited onboard computing resources of satellites present challenges for LEO constellations, hindering the timely processing of substantial amounts of accumulated user data. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a collaborative on-board processing frame- work that aims to optimize the utilization of onboard computing resources by effectively leveraging the available time window of inter-satellite links for information transfer and collaborative processing. To model this onboard processing framework, we use an integer programming model. Additionally, we recommend utilizing a simulated annealing algorithm to efficiently allocate computing resources. This algorithm has demonstrated its effi- ciency in addressing the resource allocation problem within the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Coupling Simulation of the Separation Characteristics of a “Mussel Type” Elastic Fairing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: To enhance our understanding of the influence of shell elasticity on the separation dynamics of hypersonic bivalve-type projectiles, this study employs a numerical simulation approach integrating RBD/CSD/CFD. The method successfully yields highly precise simulations, capturing the intricacies of the bidirectional coupling among aerodynamics, structural dynamics, and projectile motion. The investigation, centered on separation motion characteristics, aerodynamic forces, and shell deformation, conducts a comprehensive comparative analysis under varying conditions of dynamic pressure and structural stiffness. Results reveal a gradual increase in the significance of shell elasticity's impact on the separation process with elevated shell dynamic pressure or reduced structural stiffness. Notably, dynamic pressure exhibits a more pronounced effect compared to structural stiffness, yet neither exerts a decisive influence on the elastic bivalve-type separation process.

articleTitle: Research of Modeling Method of Automatic Flight Control System FMCP Windows
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The auto-flight system of modern civil aircraft is the main man-machine interaction system, and its flight mode operation function is jointly completed by FMCP hardware and auto-flight control system software, in order to achieve complex flight mode operation control function design, We take the FMCP window module as an example to decompose the functional hierarchy and model architecture of the complex flight mode operation function, and then form the final FMCP window model by integration each functional module, and then integrating the functional module according to the mode architecture. Finally, the model is integrated with the automatic flight control system software to verify the accuracy of the model.

articleTitle: Research on Airworthiness Verification Technology of Minimum Control Speed on the Ground for Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Minimum control speed on the ground (VMCG) is one of the top risk flight tests. This paper interprets the requirements for VMCG of Civil Aviation Regulation of China Part 25 (CCAR 25.149(e)). This paper focuses on the experience of the airworthiness certification of a civil trunk aircraft, referred to as Aircraft X, and formulates the compliance flight test techniques. The result of the VMCG compliance flight test for Aircraft X is analyzed and processed, and the VMCG data in the entire flight envelope is calculated using the flight test data and engine performance data provided by the engine manufacturer. The flight test techniques, data processing method, and data expansion method proposed in this paper can be used as a reference for future airworthiness certification of other aircraft.

articleTitle: Research and Simulation of 3D Force Transducers for Aerodynamic Testing of Ornithopters
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The three-dimensional force sensor aerodynamic test plays a crucial role in verifying the design method of hummingbird flapping wing aircraft and optimizing and improving the system characteristic parameters of the aircraft. A newly developed three-dimensional force sensor with low cost, simple structure and high performance is introduced, which is used in the aerodynamic test platform of flapping wing aircraft, and the design and static calibration method of three-dimensional force sensor are introduced. Firstly, the feasibility of the structural design of the test platform is verified by the microvariable kinematics modeling of the elastic mechanism. Then, the decoupling calibration experiment of the test platform was carried out, and the nonlinearity error of the sensor was less than1.25 %, the coupling error was less than 3.16%, and the sensitivity was greater than 1.1V/N. Finally, through the aerodynamic test of a smaller hummingbird micro-flapping wing vehicle, the quantitative evaluation data of the aerodynamic force of such a miniature flapping wing aircraft with the change of influencing parameters was obtained, which provided effective help for the indoor and outdoor flight and maneuverable flight of the micro-flapping wing.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Aerospace Equipment Based Materials Research Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Aiming to address the challenges faced by aerospace equipment encountering a series of problems such as high overload, high temperature, and susceptibility to oxidative corrosion, as well as the low efficiency of traditional experimental research and development methods during actual usage, this paper utilizes first-principle density functional theory calculations and machine learning technology to establish a material database and predict material properties. Through first-principle calculations, we can gather a large amount of material data to construct a comprehensive material database; the use of machine learning technology based on the material database to predict the materials we need to save a lot of R & D time. The results indicate that the predicted values are in line with the actual range of values.

articleTitle: Research on Assembly Visualization of Aircraft Components Driven by Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The separation of digital information from physical entities in traditional aircraft components assembly is not conducive to the understanding, judgment and execution of on-site operators, resulting in lower assembly efficiency and quality. Digital twin drive aircraft components assembly has significant advantages. This paper explores the assembly visualization of aircraft components based on digital twin, designing the technical architecture in combination with assembly requirements, refining key models through 3D point cloud surface reconstruction and assembly semantic modeling technology, realizing assembly visualization based on augmented reality technology, and finally verifying the feasibility of the digital twin-driven aircraft component assembly visualization technology through simulation. The technology basically meets the assembly requirements of aircraft components, effectively realizes visual guidance for the assembly process and achieves efficient and high-quality assembly of aircraft components.

articleTitle: Research on Methods for Analysis and Planning of Complex Multi-Satellite Missions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Satellites observation capabilities and load usage patterns are different between each other, making it difficult to the planning of multi-satellite coordinated observation missions. To address this issue, a multi-satellite complex mission operation system architecture and analysis method are proposed. Firstly, a flexible and advanced system architecture is proposed, which based on cloud computing technology and used a layered architecture. Secondly, the satellite-ground resource capacity model and the matching knowledge base are constructed. Besides, a mission scenario knowledge base is established from multiple dimensions. Finally, we take into account mission priorities, and perform intelligent matching between user requirements and resource capabilities based on the satellite-ground resource capability model and the matching knowledge base. The experimental results show that the proposed scheme can effectively improve the observation efficiency of the multi-satellite missions and can satisfy the user observation requirement with low time cost.

articleTitle: Parameter Decomposition Model for Aircraft Air Conditioning Unit Considering Low-Flow Air Paths
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Three-wheel bootstrap high-pressure water-separated air conditioning unit (ACU) is widely employed in aircraft environmental control system. To guide the design of its sub-components, performance requirement at the ACU level must be decomposed to the component level. Conventional parameter decomposition models often neglect the design of air paths with low mass flow rates inside the ACU, which will result in a deviated temperature distribution and a limited design margin for component performance. This paper introduces a parameter decomposition model that takes into account the low-flow air paths of ACU, elevating the model accuracy of temperature to within ± 2°C. To support the rational allocation of each component performance during parameter decomposition, a sensitivity analysis was conducted to identify the impact of efficiency improvements in key components on the ACU discharge temperature. Additionally, a quantitative analysis was performed to assess the influence of considering low-flow air paths on the calculation results. The study proposes a redundancy recommendation for setting ACU outlet temperature during preliminary design when low-flow air paths cannot be precisely determined.

articleTitle: Model Based Aircraft Thrust Reverse System Design
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The reverse thrust system is closely related to the takeoff/landing performance and safety characteristic of the civil aircraft. Thus the design of the reverse thrust system is one of the difficulties in the integration design of aircraft and engine. Traditional document based civil aircraft design method is not able to accurately capture the relationship between reverse thrust system and aircraft and is easy to result in design errors. This article proposes a model-based aircraft design method, and uses this method to design the thrust reverse system, achieving accurate design expression and design transfer, improving the design quality of the thrust reverse system, and reducing the risk of project rework.

articleTitle: Application of Magnetically Suspended Control Sensitive Gyroscope to Small-Angle Attitude Maneuvers of Satellites
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of Magnetically Suspended Control Sensitive Gyroscope(MSCSG) space application, the attitude maneuvering capability of spacecraft based on MSCSG is studied. On the basis of introducing the principles of MSCSG moment output and attitude sensitivity, a spacecraft attitude dynamics model based on MSCSG is established, and the PD decoupling control rate as well as the rotor maneuvering rate are designed to realize the three-axis attitude control under the saturated state of rotor deflection. The simulation results show that under the control of a single MSCSG, the satellite is able to achieve a 10° attitude maneuver in 7 seconds under the saturated MSCSG rotor deflection. Due to the characteristics of the integrated MSCSG measurement and control, it provides a new idea for the attitude maneuvering of high-orbit satellites.

articleTitle: Application of Genetic Algorithm to the Problem of Planning on Aircraft Test Procedure
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: On aircraft test procedure (abbreviate as OATP) is a kind of test which performed on the ground after the installation of aircraft cables, equipment, or systems. It aims at checking whether the installation, connection, and function of the cables, equipment, or systems are correct. It is an important part of the integration verification work. Whether the testing of aircraft type can be well planned is closely linked with the entire OATP testing process and testing process often related to these factors such as the number of tests, the costs, and efficiency, these factors will determine the cycle of the entire validation process and thus affect the entire development work for an aircraft type. Therefore, it is necessary to combined with the resources of flight testing and the test relationships to plan the logical sequence of OATP testing based on the independence of different systems and the their influence level on aircraft functions and related systems. Based on the limitations that summarized from the development experience, adjust the order of experimental implementation to achieve optimal resource utilization. This article creates a model that is similar to the job shop scheduling problem and explores how to use genetic algorithms iterate the logical order of tests based on the determined principles of development experience. The conclusion indicates that genetic algorithm is an efficient way to deal with the OATP test planning problem.

articleTitle: Dynamic SPO Mode Air-Ground Cooperative Task Allocation Strategy Based on DQN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Single Pilot Operation (SPO) mode is an important development direction for future commercial airplanes, but the SPO mode faces problems such as ambiguous definition of adaptive intelligent driving modes, and task allocation problems under specific modes and multi-condition constraints. In this paper, we consider the task allocation needs due to the change of human-machine loop in SPO mode, firstly, we analyze the air-ground cooperative architecture of SPO mode, and define four driving modes; secondly, we establish the task allocation model of air-ground cooperative architecture of SPO mode based on the method of deep Q-network (DQN), which contains the number of intelligences, the task requirements, resource space constraints and other multi-conditions. Finally, numerical simulation shows that the method solves the problem of limited dynamic allocation of resources considering the task demand in SPO mode and multiple constraints, which verifies the correctness and usability of the model.

articleTitle: Trajectory Planning for Aircraft in Complex No-Fly Zones Based on Hybrid A * Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A complex trajectory planning method for aircraft in no-fly zone based on hybrid A * algorithm is proposed. A hybrid A * algorithm is used to represent the no-fly zone discretely, which makes up the shortage of the traditional circular no-fly zone representation. The optimal turning radius and step size in the hybrid A * algorithm are computed using a genetic algorithm to generate waypoints for the aircraft's flight path and perform path planning. The energy consumption of the trajectory is taken as the evaluation index, and the trajectory planning is completed by combining the dynamics model of the aircraft. The simulation results show that the design method can simplify the trajectory planning of aircraft in the complex no-fly zone into geometric path planning and trajectory planning combined with kinematic model, and the aircraft can successfully avoid the no-fly zone, which verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Research on Stereo Mapping Technology of Optical Satellite Based on SLAM
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Currently, optical satellite stereo mapping technology has become the main means of large and medium scale terrain mapping. However, the realization of high-resolution satellite stereo mapping is inseparable from the continuous progress of high-precision mapping processing technology. In this paper, three typical mapping methods and characteristics of optical satellites are firstly analyzed, and a single linear array satellite mapping processing technology based on Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) is proposed. Finally, a model is established through simulation experiments for error analysis, and the feasibility of the application of this technology in single linear array agile stereo mode satellite is obtained.

articleTitle: Navigation Performance Analysis for GPS/BDS-3 Users with Interfered Observations
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) has provided Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) services to global users. However, in military confrontations, satellite constellations often face various scenarios of failure, including interference, deception, and attacks. It is crucial to analyze the performance of navigation services in satellite failure conditions. It is imperative to simulate satellite failure scenarios and investigate the navigation and positioning performance of global satellite systems under partial satellite failures caused by interference observations. Additionally, it is necessary to analyze the impact of different satellite failure scenarios on the navigation performance. Results show that as the number of satellite failures increases, the positioning accuracy and the number of visible satellites decrease. In the case of BDS-3/GPS, the change in navigation performance is superior to that of BDS-3 alone.

articleTitle: Stable Domain for Geocentric GWs Observatory Based on Deviation Boundary Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The drift of in the orbital elements between spacecraft directly affects the stability of triangular constellations, which in turn leads to the apparent instability in part of the parameter design space. This paper investigates the stable domain of the geocentric gravitational waves (GWs) constellation configuration considering the stability constraints. Select breathing angle index as stability criteria through analysis. Using the univariate method, the geometric relationship between the arm length and the orbital elements of spacecraft in a triangular configuration is analyzed to determine the orbital element deviation boundaries. Furthermore, numerical integration is adopted to determine the natural evolution extremum of the omnidirectional geocentric configuration during the mission period, and the most sensitive orbital elements are determined. The deviation boundary delineates certain unstable and quasi stable domains in the omnidirectional parameter design space. The proposed method can potentially be useful for constellation design and optimization.

articleTitle: Reliability Analysis of eVTOL Avionics System Architecture Based on Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: As the low-altitude economy grows, electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft are heralding a revolutionary phase in urban air mobility (UAM) due to their unique characteristics. Avionics, being a critical infrastructure component of these aircraft, necessitate the exploration and development of a new generation of avionic system architectures specifically for eVTOL. This paper presents an avionics system architecture tailored for UAM scenarios. It conducts a reliability analysis of this system architecture by converting fault trees into bayesian network models. The analysis, based on fault probability and posterior probability, concludes that the proposed avionics system architecture possesses high reliability. This study is instrumental in guiding the development of avionics for both eVTOL and unmanned aerial vehicles.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Function Requirements Validation Process for Civil Aircrafts Based on ARP 4754A
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The application of ARP 4754A-based Function Requirements Validation Process (FRVP) for civil aircrafts ensures the integrity and rationality of verifying aircraft-level requirements, and facilitates the fidelity of aircraft-level requirements definition. The Top-Down design of aircraft-level FRVP is carried out in this study based on ARP 4754A. By employing methods such as requirements review, requirements trace, and requirements analysis, the process of validating these requirements is presented. Furthermore, each step involved in the validation is studied in depth to ensure their completeness, correctness, and rationality.

articleTitle: Analysis of Self-Excited Vibration in Multi-Wheel Brake Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The hydraulic braking system is one of the key functional subsystems that affect the safety of aircraft take off and landing[1]. The vibration of the barking system can lead to damage to the hydraulic pipelines and equipment failures, causing safety problems of aircraft takeoff and landing [2]–[3]. This paper built mathematical models for the vibration problem that occurred during the test of a certain type of aircraft braking system and also, simulation analysis and research were conducted. Through the research, it was found that the vibration mechanism of the braking system was a type of nonlinear self-excited vibration with positive feedback. Improvement solutions for the braking system were proposed, and a preliminary assessment of the stability margin of the improved system was conducted.

articleTitle: SQP-Based Multi-Objective Optimization Using Approximate Gradient
