publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In the engineering environment, aerodynamic design tends to face the problem of finding the optimal value under multiple objectives and multiple constraints, so the huge computational cost expenditure which mainly caused by enormous repeated gradient calculations becomes the biggest obstacle for the application of aerodynamic optimization. In this paper, an efficient optimization method using approximate gradient analysis was proposed to save gradient calculation time, in which the objective functions were evaluated with high-fidelity analyses in one-dimensional linear search, while the gradients were evaluated with a less time-consuming approximation model during the optimization process. Multi-objective problems were handled with linear weighted sum method. Multi-objective aerodynamic optimization performed on RAE2822 airfoil were investigated. Compared to standard SQP (sequential quadratic programming) optimization, the presented method yields 66.2% CPU time reduction for two-point airfoil design. The study indicates that the proposed optimization procedure has significant potential for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Calculation Method of the Ground Backflip Weight and Center of Gravity Limitation for Civil Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: During the normal ground shutdown and ground operation (loading, unloading and equipment disassembly) of the aircraft, the vertical load of the nose landing gear will change with the change of the weight and the center of gravity for the aircraft. When the current vertical load of the nose landing gear is less than the critical value, the aircraft may have the risk of backflip. Based on the Actual operation and use scenarios of civil aircraft, this paper proposed the environmental factor model and the reasonable principle of determining vertical load of the nose landing gear for the first time, established the analysis model, and determined the calculation method about the weight and the center of gravity limitation of the ground backflip for conventional aircraft layout (fixed wing, retractable landing gear at the front three points, wing-suspended engine and conventional tail layout), which provides a reasonable calculation method for the safety of the weight and the center of gravity on ground operation of civil aircraft.

Author Keywords: weight and the center of gravity limitation

articleTitle: Research on Joint Simulation of Hydraulic System of Transport Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The transportation hydraulic system is the most important secondary energy of aircraft, and the reasonable configuration of the hydraulic system architecture directly affects the safety, reliability, economy and other indicators of aircraft. In this paper, an analysis method based on AMESim platform is proposed, which starts from the demand of hydraulic users, reasonably allocates hydraulic pump source, and verifies the demand of hydraulic users for hydraulic pressure on the premise of meeting the flow demand of hydraulic users.

articleTitle: Vessel Trajectory Tracking and Intention Recognition Algorithm Under Multi-Source Satellite Situation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Space-based joint situation awareness encompasses three sources: on-board perception, ground-based annotation, and inter-satellite communication. This paper primarily investigates key areas such as multi-source satellite situation perception, situation fusion, situation understanding, and situation prediction. We utilize an enhanced Kalman filter algorithm and the K-nearest neighbors algorithm. These algorithms enable us to autonomously generate search and discovery, identify target types, predict target trajectories based on positioning and movement, conduct multi-target association, and perform data fusion simulations. Additionally, we employ CART decision trees and random forest algorithms to comprehensively infer target threat levels. Finally, by establishing simulation scenarios for suspicious activities in a specific maritime area, the feasibility of the aforementioned methods is validated.

articleTitle: Debris Threat Assessment Algorithm Based on Multiple-Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: For the space debris avoidance, a threat assessment method based on multiple-factors is proposed. First on the basis of the traditional rendezvous distance as the main judgement factor, the remaining rendezvous time and the current distance are added as threat factors, and the influence of each factor on the threat assessment is analyzed. Then the three rendezvous influencing factors are unified to establish the multiple-factor, and the threat evaluation model is designed with the multiple-factor, and finally the calculation method and process of the threat evaluation model are given. Simulation experiments show that the evaluation algorithm further specify the threat value of the debris to spacecraft.

articleTitle: Correlation Analysis of Aircraft State Parameters Based on Telemetry Data
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The telemetry data reflects the state of aircraft. It is of great significance for state interpretation, abnormal state detection and applause analysis to deeply analyze and find the correlation between parameters in telemetry data. The flight state of the aircraft is divided into motion state, environmental state and equipment working state according to the physical information reflected by telemetry data. In this paper, the correlation coefficient calculation method is designed, which combines the PRE (proportional reduction of error) method and the distance correlation method. On this basis, a typical flight data of long-endurance aircraft is selected. The correlation coefficient of two parameters is calculated by the design method. The correlation between different types of parameters is given. Among them, this paper focuses on the analysis of the correlation between irradiation intensity and pitch angle, solar array output current and aircraft surface temperature, solar array output current and pitch angle.

articleTitle: A High-Frequency Excitation and Vibration Test System for Turbine Blades in Aviation Rotors
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Turbomachine rotor blades may rupture under high-frequency excitation if not manufactured properly, leading to rotor and machine failure. To understand the impact of such excitations on the structure and fatigue performance of rotor blades, it is essential to subject them to high-frequency tests. The frequency of these excitations can exceed 10 kHz for rotors, necessitating a high-frequency test system. Additionally, as working rotors rotate, measuring the vibratory response of rotor blades becomes challenging, often requiring expensive instruments. This paper presents the design of a simple, high-frequency excitation and test system to stimulate rotor blades and measure their response. In this system, tested blades remain stationary while the excitation airflow rotates, ensuring relative motion between the excitation source and the blades. The system can generate up to 18.8 kHz high-frequency excitation, enabling non-contact excitation and measurement since the blades are stationary, thereby avoiding the addition of mass to the test blades, as seen in some other methods. The composition of the test bench is introduced first, including the exciter subsystem, the measuring subsystem, and the tested rotor. The design of the rotating airflow exciter is then described in detail. The effectiveness of this system is verified through an acceleration/deceleration transient excitation test on a rotor blade of an aviation turbine. Experimental results demonstrate that this system can effectively excite the first six order modes of this blade and measure its response.

articleTitle: Research on Close-Range Collision Avoidance Guideline for Spacecraft
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In view of the problem of close-range collision avoidance in the space navigation of the two spacecraft, by the VVLH relative orbit coordinate system, “high lift and low drop” avoidance guideline is proposed. The application of this guideline on two spacecraft can make the spacecraft with high orbit height lift and the spacecraft with low orbit height drop, so as to widen the relative distance between the two to achieve avoidance. Applied to two high orbit spacecraft close-range collision scenarios, the trajectory simulation results show that this Guideline can effectively realize the collision avoidance of spacecraft.

articleTitle: Assessment of Missile Warning Effectiveness for Local Conflicts
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: During the Russia-Ukraine conflict, both sides deployed a significant number of various missile weapons, with the first deployment of hypersonic weapons. The missile warning systems of both sides provided varying degrees of informational support. This paper initially analyzes and elaborates on the composition of the missile warning systems of both Russia and Ukraine. Through simulation and evaluation, the paper assesses the effectiveness of the missile warning systems of both sides. The results indicate that the missile warning systems of Ukraine and NATO excel in anti-missile action support compared to the Russian missile warning system.

articleTitle: Force Planning for Anti-UAV Protection Tasks of Power Grid via Grouping Competitive Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A force demand planning method based on grouping-based swarm optimization algorithm (GCSO) is proposed for the anti-VAV swarm protection task of the grid. Firstly, based on information such as the escort radius, maneuverability, enemy VAV attack coverage, and maneuver-ability of the escort device, a mathematical model for large-scale power grid escort task force demand planning is constructed; Then, a competitive learning swarm optimization algorithm based on grouping idea is proposed, which divides the particle swarm into three subpopulations according to the average fitness size, and different subpopulations compete with each other to fully develop the optimization ability of the particle swarm; Simulation experiments have shown that this algorithm can effectively improve the planning quality of anti VAV escort forces for escort devices, and can effectively enhance the scheduling efficiency of power grid escort systems.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Verification of SAR Antenna in Near-Lunar Orbit
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The complex heat flux environment and the wide range of infrared variation of the Moon are a challenge to the thermal design of the outer spacecraft in the Moon orbit. In this paper, combined with the characteristics of the orbit, the heat flow environment of the near-lunar orbit is analyzed in detail, the thermal analysis of the extravehicular load under this environment is carried out, the difficulties of the thermal design of the lunar environment are analyzed, and the heat flow simulation method is designed to simulate transient and dramatic infrared radiation. The thermal control of a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) antenna is designed and the thermal balance test is carried out. The test results show that the antenna can withstand the test of extreme operating conditions and the temperature of each unit meets the requirements of the index. This paper has certain reference significance for the thermal control design of satellite-carrying synthetic aperture radar antenna.

articleTitle: A Calibration Method for Magnetic Levitation Control Model of Space Vibration Isolation System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for calibrating a terrestrial electromagnetic force output model. The method employs high-precision measuring instruments for testing, choosing a mode of independent model detection and spatial pose transformation. It calculates the electromagnetic force between the electromagnet components and the exciter coils to obtain the control force output parameters of the entire levitation experiment system. This helps to improve the capability level of magnetic levitation control in the levitation experiment system. The correctness of the electromagnetic force model was verified through ground air-bearing tests of the levitation experiment system, and supported the effectiveness and accuracy of closed-loop control data.

articleTitle: New Rotor Maneuvering Technology Based on Biefeld-Brown Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: An unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is a type of vehicle that has no crew and has a significant role in both military and life fields, but in life, the operation of UAVs tends to cause greater noise, and high-speed rotating blades can pose a hazard to pedestrians. To reduce UAV noise as well as enhance safety, a novel rotor maneuvering technique based on the Biefeld-Brown effect is adopted in this paper. The technology eliminates the use of electric motors, requiring only the shaft and bearings that support the blades, producing lift after high voltage electricity is applied. This article also carried on the experiment to the device which utilized this technology, obtained the relations between the lift, the voltage and the rotational speed; It is shown that there is a form of lift in this technique, and that the position relation of the two electrodes can make the propeller produce faster rotational speed if it is internal and external relation, and larger non rotating lift if it is up and down relation; The hollowed out net like duct was designed and proved to be better than the traditional tube like duct by experiment; The coaxial contra rotating propeller structure is designed and the performance is proved to be better than single propeller by tests.

articleTitle: Robust Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification for UAVs During Fast Fading Channels
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Radio frequency fingerprint (RFF) identification is an emerging device authentication technique that leverages hardware imperfections arising from the manufacturing process. Due to the strong time-varying characteristics of the UAV channels, it is difficult to apply the existing RFF identification methods to the UAV. In this paper, we propose a data augmentation method on the raw IQ signal, which use to enhance the robustness of the pre-trained model when extracting RFF in the presence of severe fast fading in the real flight environment. By employing this technique, we are able to extract robust features on the UAV signals. We evaluated the performance of our method in diverse environments, including UAV hovering state and moving state. In the hovering and moving state of UAV, using data augmentation can improve the average recognition accuracy by 8.2%.

articleTitle: A Simplified 2D-Model for Satellite Cooling Control Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) is an emerging control technique to solve optimal control problems. In this work, we develop a data-driven control approach that uses the DRL technique to intelligently design an effective strategy for operating the satellite cooling system. First, we construct a two-dimensional dynamic thermal environment for satellite panels by numerical simulation. Secondly, we employ an Artificial Neural Network, trained via a DRL agent, to execute satellite thermal control. Subsequently, we assess the agent's performance under extreme temperature conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that our method can effectively reduce the cumulative extreme temperature in simulation environments by 28%, 25%, and 13% respectively, compared to the traditional threshold-based approach across multiple environmental scenarios. Furthermore, the proposed method demonstrates robust performance across diverse noise conditions, yielding satisfactory results. Extensive experiments indicate that the model trained with TD3, which incorporates specific noise into sensors, displays significant robustness under high noise conditions.

articleTitle: Research on Spacecraft Structural Field Nodes Temperature Interpolation Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This research paper explores the application and effects of different interpolation algorithms in the thermal-structural coupling analysis of spacecraft, particularly comparing the back propagation (BP) neural network interpolation method with the multivariate Barnes interpolation method. Through actual case test simulations, the study demonstrates that the BP neural network interpolation surpasses the traditional multivariate Barnes interpolation method in terms of accuracy and efficiency. This research provides scientific evidence for selecting interpolation strategies based on different engineering requirements.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Fault Detection and Diagnosis for Cooling Units
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In this paper, a chiller simulation model is developed for generating simulated operation data of chiller units under faulty and fault-free conditions, and the reliability of the generated simulation dataset is verified. For the experimental chiller system, fault-free and refrigerant leakage and condenser water flow reduction fault simulation experiments were carried out, and based on the experimental data, a chiller refrigerant charge model was established using the joint modeling approach of physical modeling, empirical modeling, and data-driven modeling, and the experimental data were used to verify the accuracy of the system simulation model. The results show that after digital twinning, the maximum relative errors of all thermal parameters of the system simulation model do not exceed 5.5%, and the correct rate of the positive and fault diagnosis model is increased by 5%.

articleTitle: An Evolvable Swarm-Parallel Algorithm Framework for Satellite-Ground Networking Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Satellite Internet has been deployed rapidly, leading to an explosive growth in satellite scale, further strengthening the contradiction between the growing demand for satellite-ground communication and the limited ground station resources. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an evolvable swarm-parallel algorithm framework (ESPAF), which comprises a swarm-parallel solving and deconflicting framework, a learning-assisted metaheuristic (LM) fast-solving algorithm that combines reinforcement learning (RL) and Tabu simulated annealing (TSA), and a linear programming (LP) exact-solving algorithm. The ESPAF breaks through the traditional task-driven satellite scheduling approach found in existing research and presents a novel and appropriate method for optimizing satellite-ground networking under a new macro paradigm. A series of experimental instances involving up to 1,000 satellites and 100 ground stations demonstrate the efficient performance of ESPAF. Comparative experiments with alternative metaheuristic algorithms and the CPLEX solver further emphasized ESP AF's ability to generate high-quality solutions more rapidly.

articleTitle: Fault Propagation Analysis and Optimum Placement of Sensors for Fault Diagnosis Based on Combined Weighting-TOPSIS Method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Mechanical transmission systems are widely used in the aerospace field, but its incipient fault characteristic periodic signals are in low frequency band and often buried in the noise, so those senors placed in the system should be used to collect abundance of sensitive features in order to acquire more fault signals and monitor fault development stations to minimize the losses. A method of fault propagation analysis and optimum placement of sensors in mechanical transmission systems based on combined weighting-TOPSIS (Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution) are proposed in this paper. Those fault development curves for typical fault modes would be generated by those sensors placed in the system, and then the abilities of each sensor to collect fault signals and monitor the development of faults can be calculated. Finally, a combined weighting-TOPSIS method is used to solve the problem of sensors layout and localization, and provide a method to determine the optimal number and position of sensors. This method proposed in this paper can efficiently realize the process of optimal sensor placement in order to improve the precision of fault diagnosis for mechanical transmission systems.

articleTitle: In Orbit Testing Accuracy Analysis of Communication Satellite Transponders
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: After the launch and orbit determination of high orbit satellites, in orbit testing of satellite transponders will be carried out. In the past testing process, after the completion of the test, it was only possible to simply compare the test results to see if they met the technical requirements. The accuracy of in orbit testing directly affects the accuracy of satellite payload related indicators testing results. By analyzing the error components of various tests during the in orbit testing process, obtained the testing accuracy of typical test items during in orbit testing. Further optimization can be carried out for specific error components, further improve the accuracy of in orbit testing of satellite repeater related indicators.

articleTitle: Research on Airworthiness Compliance of Civil Aircraft Air Conditioning System with APU Bleed
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The purpose of assessing airworthiness compliance for the air conditioning system is to determine whether the fresh air and cabin environment comply with APU bleed regulations. Currently, in the design of civil aircraft, APU bleed airflow is calculated based on the minimum fresh air required by airworthiness regulations. However, under extreme conditions, such as on extremely hot days, the fresh air provided by the air conditioning system under failure conditions may not meet the minimum fresh air required by airworthiness regulations. Insufficient fresh air can adversely affect passengers' behavior and health. Therefore, this paper proposes an airworthiness compliance method that is based on the minimum fresh air required per person according to airworthiness regulations. This method comprises assessments of the CO2 concentration in the cabin and the core temperature of the human body to demonstrate the compliance of the air conditioning system with APU bleed.

articleTitle: Different Orbit Plane Reconstruction Strategy Using Continuous Low Thrusts
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Conventional theoretical models under impulse thrust conditions are unable to realize the control of Right Ascension of Ascending Node (RAAN) reconfiguration of different orbit plane under continuous low thrust conditions. In this paper, the orbital dynamics formula under continuous low thrust is derived, which can calculate the velocity increment required to change the RAAN with continuous low thrust. Simulation validation reveals that the energy required for RAAN reconfiguration control under continuous low thrust is inversely proportional to the orbital altitude and directly proportional to the orbital inclination and RAAN separation. For LEO spacecraft, the velocity increment consumed for a 10° RAAN separation is within 100 m/s. The reconfiguration strategy under continuous low thrust conditions investigated in the paper enables a better exploration of the operational control strategy of mega constellations.

articleTitle: Efficiency of Actuation Force for Aircraft Morphing Trailing Edge
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The use of deformed trailing edge can greatly improve the aerodynamic characteristics and stealth performance of aircraft. Improving the driving efficiency of aircraft can reduce energy loss and improve flight efficiency. In order to investigate the effect of magnitude and direction of actuation force on the deflection of the trailing edge, the nonlinear beam model for the morphing trailing edge is developed and the finite difference method is used. Results show that the direction of the actuation force has a powerful effect on the deflection of a cantilever beam. The direction has been found to maximize the tip displacement when the actuation force is applied with a given magnitude. The minimum actuation force is almost perpendicular to the tangent to the deflection curve at the point of application. Numerical and experimental results show the loading case in which the actuation force is always perpendicular to the line tangent to the deflection curve shows high efficiency. It provides a guideline to design the actuation system for morphing trailing edge.

articleTitle: Analysis and Research of Abnormal Output Failure of Data Terminal Processor
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The data terminal processor completes the information collection and calculation with the subsystems of the aircraft electromechanical system, and interacts with the upper computer display system at the same time, effectively improving the performance of the aircraft platform and improving the level of health management. This paper mainly analyzes and studies the abnormal output mechanism of the data terminal processor, investigates and locates the illegal address access and reset causes caused by the abnormal output, and finally puts forward the problem solution, and puts forward optimization and improvement measures for the output control logic of the data terminal processor. It provides important support for the normal operation of data terminal processors and the safety and reliability of aircraft electromechanical systems.

articleTitle: Preliminary Design of BDS Emergency Warning Service
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Emergency Warning Service is a specialized service that delivers critical information within navigation messages. Beidou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) also plans to deploy EWS. This paper presents an overview of the Emergency Warning service, outlines its key characteristics, proposes some potential solutions for implementing this service in BDS, conducts a comparative analysis among these methods, discusses some multi-GNSS inter-operation concerns, and gives some recommendations.

articleTitle: Energy Strategy Optimization of Serial Turbine Hybrid-Electric Based on Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In this paper, based on the characteristics of serial turbine hybrid-electric architecture, firstly the propulsion system and platform load power requirements of the flight profile are analyzed, and the output power of the power system is analyzed, and then the preliminary design of the serial turbine hybrid-electric power system is completed with the quality characteristics of the power battery, generator and fuel consumption combined with the power demand. Compared with the original fuel aircraft, the fuel consumption decreased by 46.4 %, but the total quality of the power system was much higher than that of the original fuel aircraft. Finally, the power hybridization ratio was defined and the weight model was combined to find the optimal parameter group. Based on the particle swarm optimization algorithm, the parameters a, WBAT and tICE of the serial turbine hybrid-electric power system were optimized, and combined to complete the design of the serial turbine hybrid-electric power system. Experience shows that although fuel consumption is increased by 2.6% before optimization, the total quality of the power system is reduced by about 36%, and the whole machine has greatly improved the quality benefit under the premise of small sacrifice economy, leaving plenty of room for further improvement and optimization.

articleTitle: Research on the Method of Hotspot Identification for Conflict Situations at Longdongbao Airport
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of the domestic civil aviation industry, there has been a notable increase in the frequency of conflicts and runway incursions during the taxiing process of aircraft at multi-runway airports, which has seriously affected the efficiency and safety of airport operations. As a result, identifying and delineating conflict hots pots on the airport surface has become one of the key concerns in domestic airport management. This study takes the dual-runway operation mode of Guiyang Longdongbao Airport as a case to explore the construction of an airport surface structure model. Due to the complexity of the Longdongbao Airport system under multi-runway operation mode, this paper adopts the “node-link” model for simplification and modeling, dividing it into three main parts: taxiway system, apron system, and runway system. The modeling methods and specific processes for these parts are introduced in detail. The paper further records the details of the arrival and departure flights at Guiyang Longdongbao Airport on February 9th, and uses the frequency of node occupancy and actual operation data of the airport surface to filter out suspected conflict hot spots. By combining the operational data and the identified suspected hot spots, the paper applies stepwise regression analysis to further analyze the conflict hot spots and validate the findings. Predictions are also made on the number of conflicts that may occur per unit time, which helps pilots and controllers to anticipate potential conflicts and collisions, thereby enhancing the efficiency and safety of airport operations.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Small Land-Air Amphibious Spherical Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Multifunctional small special robots have broad application prospects. Aiming at the application fields of detection, inspection and investigation in complex and dangerous areas, a small amphibious spherical robot is designed, which can realize autonomous mode conversion between land rolling and aerial flight. The land rolling mode adopts the design of a hamster-cage-like drive scheme. The flight mode is a side-by-side rotor aircraft, and the motion mode conversion is controlled by the arm angle steering engine. The structural design of the motion platform avoids the problem of redundancy caused by function superposition through component function reuse, and improves the compactness of the structure (the overall size is a partial sphere with a diameter of 16.4 cm, and a total weight of only 514 g). In order to verify the feasibility of the configuration design of the robot motion platform, the 3D modeling software is used to construct the 3D model of the whole machine. Then, to verify the robot's motion characteristics, the dynamics model of the robot is deduced and built, and the motion characteristic parameter analysis and aerodynamic simulation are carried out. Finally, a multi-degree-of-freedom experimental bench is built, and the experimental tests and parameter debugging are carried out by using the physical prototype of the robot to achieve the expected design goals. The research results validate the effectiveness of the robot's design, with performance index meeting the preset requirements, providing a reference for the design of amphibious spherical robots.

articleTitle: Angle-Only Orbit Determination Method for Cislunar Orbits Under Observational Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Cislunar space, due to its special dynamical properties, is an ideal location for space missions. High-accuracy orbit determination (OD) is a prerequisite to guarantee the successful implementation of cislunar space missions. The resources for observations of cislunar space are limited, impacting the OD performances. In this paper, an angle-only OD method is proposed for cislunar space under restricted observation conditions. Firstly, an angle-only OD model for cislunar space is established, and a local observability assessment method based on the Fisher matrix is proposed. Secondly, the observability of the ang-only OD in the cislunar space is analyzed based on the proposed local observability assessment method. A strategy for OD under restricted observation conditions is proposed to improve OD accuracy. Finally, the proposed method is successfully applied to solve the OD problem of a Near Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO). The accuracy of OD under the same observation conditions is analyzed. Simulation results indicate that this method can effectively improve the accuracy of OD under restricted observation conditions. The proposed method can be potentially useful in future cislunar missions.

articleTitle: Derivation and Simulation of Beidou System QMBOC Signal Distortion Model
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: This study examines the distortion characteristics of the QMBOC (Quadrature Multiplexed Binary Offset Carrier) modulation signal. The QMBOC ideal signal creation formula extends the digital and analog distortion model suited for QMBOC by mathematical modeling, based on the 2-OS distortion model and BOC distortion model. The legend is then generated using a simulation platform. The inconsistency in the weight proportion of the distortion of the in-phase and orthogonal components of the QMBOC signal is attributed to the γ power factor of the signal. The simulation results indicate that the primary signal distortion is primarily associated with the Q branch in the investigation and examination of the duty ratio and distortion value. Additionally, the simulation analysis of distortion also supports the corresponding experimental findings. This offers a theoretical backing for examining the distortion properties of QMBOC.

articleTitle: Ontology-Based Mission Analysis and Planning Framework for External Multi-Payload System of Space Station
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Space station supports various space science research with multi-payloads outside its platform. Characterized by concurrent and intersecting missions alongside intricate constraints, mission planning technology is vital for ensuring scientific returns from multidisciplinary payloads. Mission analysis and framework design are fundamental for effective planning. This paper addresses the challenges of mission analysis and planning framework design for space station external payload missions. Firstly, based on mission planning theory and the characteristics of multidisciplinary missions, we introduce a mission requirement description model using ontology theory. This model enables a standardized description of missions across various disciplines and is validated through typical mission descriptions. Next, we analyze planning elements to describe the issue in multi-payload mission planning, transforming the problem into a combinatorial optimization problem. Finally, we propose a segmented and centralized planning framework with feedback mechanisms. Its effectiveness is confirmed through qualitative analysis, offering a theoretical and practical basis for multi-payload mission planning.

articleTitle: Research on Control of Micro Turbojet Engine Based on All-Coefficient Adaptive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the 150kg thrust stage micro turbojet engine has strong nonlinearity in the starting, acceleration and deceleration process under complex environment, is susceptible to external interference, and too long operation time leads to component aging and system time-varying. An all-coefficient adaptive control (ACAC) method based on characteristic model is proposed. It avoids the defect that the traditional proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller cannot adjust adaptively when facing the nonlinear time-varying system. Firstly, based on the ground test data of the micro turbojet engine, a simple empirical mathematical model (including the rotational speed model and thrust model) is established by using deep neural network method, and the accuracy of the model can reach 96.8%. Secondly, the control effect of ACAC algorithm and PID control algorithm on thrust is compared by simulation. The results show that the adjustment time of ACAC control algorithm is 0.05 s and 0.04s higher than that of PID when the system has disturbance and the system gain changes. It is verified that the method has better rapidity and strong anti-disturbance ability, which provides important engineering value for the selection of control strategies to improve the acceleration and deceleration characteristics of micro turbojet engines with large thrust level.

articleTitle: A Decoupled-and-Reduced Method for Configuration Uncertainty Propagation of Gravitational-Wave Observatory
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: A space-based gravitational-wave observatory usually contains three spacecraft, forming a triangle configuration in space for interferometry. Configuration stability is significant for a gravitational-wave observatory to ensure interferometry detection performance. Although a pre-designed configuration can satisfy the stability requirements, the stability can be impacted by uncertainties such as orbit insertion errors, which necessitates the investigation of configuration uncertainty propagation. Current configuration uncertainty propagation methods suffer from drawbacks related to high computational burden. To this end, this paper presents a decoupled-and-reduced method. First, a decoupled-and-reduced state transition tensor (DR-STT) is developed for orbital uncertainty propagation. The conventional STT is reduced by capturing high-order dominant secular terms. The secular and periodic terms are decoupled and integrated independently to reduce computational costs further. Then, high-order analytical derivatives are proposed to transform the uncertainties in orbital states into uncertainties in configuration stability indexes. The proposed method is successfully applied to solve the configuration uncertainty propagation problem of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna project (LISA). Simulation results show that the proposed method can provide results comparable to the conventional STT-based method, but it requires only one-third of the computational time.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a Triple-Orthogonal Magnetic Resistance Translational Bearing
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: Magnetically Suspended Universally Stabilized Platform (MSUSP) is a new spacecraft platform with six-degree-of-freedom suspension control function of translational and rotational decoupling, which can be used to improve the attitude pointing accuracy and universally agile maneuvering performance of satellite payload. In this paper., a triple-orthogonal magnetic resistance translational bearing is designed for MSUSP translational suspension control which uses a co-spherical spherical tilting-mounted magnetic poles structure in order to optimize the payload room., and is capable of decoupling the platform translational and rotational control and decoupling the electromagnetic forces of each bearing channel. The electromagnetic force characteristics of the bearing is analyzed based on the equivalent magnetic circuit method., and the electromagnetic force model linearized near the equilibrium position and the parameters such as current stiffness and displacement stiffness of the bearing are obtained. The working air gap magnetic density uniformity and electromagnetic force characteristics are analyzed by the finite element model., and the simulation results show that: the fluctuation rate of the working air gap magnetic density of the triple-orthogonal magnetic resistance translational bearing is lower than 0.2%, the electromagnetic force is linearly correlated with the control current and the displacement of the motion system., which is consistent with the calculation result of the equivalent magnetic circuit method., and the triple-orthogonal magnetic resistance translational bearing designed in this paper can meet the payload carrying requirement of the MSUSP motion system.

articleTitle: BWO-LSSVR Model-Based Aeroengine Combustor Multi-Objective Optimum Design
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: As one of the core components of aeroengine, high efficiency and high performance combustor design is the key to the high reliability operation of aeroengine and even the whole aircraft. In order to avoid the problems of long cycle and high calculation cost of traditional combustor design, the optimization design of combustor based on machine learning has achieved some results, but these methods are limited by the number of samples and are easy to fall into local optimal. In this paper, based on an aeroengine combustor model, combined with BWO-LSSVR (Beluga Optimization - least square support vector regression) model and MOSSA (multi-objective sparrow search algorithm) algorithm, the multi-objective optimization design of combustor is carried out to maximize combustion efficiency and minimize total pressure loss. The results show that, compared with SVR, LSSVR, Kriging and other common models, BWO-LSSVR model has the lowest root-mean-square error and average absolute percentage error, and has the highest prediction accuracy under the condition of small sample. The Pareto solution set and optimal design space are obtained through multi-objective optimization, which provides physical insights for advanced aero engine combustor design meeting performance indexes, and can guide the optimization design of combustor and accelerate the development of aeroengine.

articleTitle: Research on Space-Ground Two-Way Time Comparison Method Based on Carrier Phase Smoothing Pseudo-Range
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: The high-precision time-frequency system has been sent to the China Space Station(CSS), which improves the accuracy of the time-frequency reference in space and puts forward the higher requirements on the matching time comparison technology. Aiming at this demand, the carrier phase smoothing pseudo-range method is proposed to improve the accuracy of the two-way time comparison based on the pseudo-range. Aiming at the problem of cycle slip in high dynamic, this paper proposes a combination of ionospheric residual method and carrier phase difference fitting method, and analyzes its error correction method. It can detect and repair all cycle slip combinations that affect two-way time comparison. The experimental result using the observation data of the CSS shows that this method improves the accuracy of the two-way time comparison from hundreds of picoseconds to picoseconds.

articleTitle: Fast Orbit Maneuvering Optimization for Network Satellite Observations of Ground Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Symposium on Aerospace Engineering and Systems (ISAES)
abstract: When a satellite is used to perform an Earth observation mission, orbital maneuvers are important when the moving target exceeds the maximum coverage field of the satellite-lite. Fast response observation is achieved by a noncoplanar orbital maneuver. First, the minimum geocentric angle distance between the satellite point trajectory and the target point trajectory is determined via the two-body model, and the time required for the maneuvering satellite to fly over the target point is analytically obtained. On the premise of not changing the shape of the satellite orbit plane, the fastest arrival time of orbit transfer to the target is obtained. Under the condition of satisfying the maximum impulse constraint, the initial satellite orbit change time and the required velocity increments are calculated by the objective function of the minimum fuel consumption and the fastest arrival time. According to the observation of satellites maneuvering to multiple targets, the minimum impulse of satellites maneuvering to the target is obtained. The target allocation of satellites that need to maneuver to each target is performed by using zero-one integer programming. Then, the problem is transformed into an optimization of multiple satellites to single-target maneuvering, and the optimal maneuvering satellites and the required impulse of each target point are obtained.
